options.title: Seven countries claim Antarctica. None can have it
options.first_line: Countries have carved Antarctica into slices, and not one of them is allowed to keep a single piece.
options.first_frame: The white continent seen from above, coloured slices fanning out from the South Pole with seven little flags at their edges.

options.title: Antarctica is the one continent nobody owns
options.first_line: Antarctica is the one continent on the map that no country is allowed to own.
options.first_frame: The globe tilted to show the bottom of the world, Antarctica glowing blank white while every other continent is filled with countries.

options.title: Britain, Chile and Argentina all claim the same ice
options.first_line: Britain, Chile and Argentina all claim the same piece of Antarctica, and none of them can have it.
options.first_frame: The Antarctic Peninsula close up, three coloured slices drawn on top of each other in a stripy overlap with three flags planted on the same spot.

why: Three named countries claiming the very same ice, with three flags planted on one striped spot, makes a stranger ask how that is possible, while B gives the answer away and A is vaguer.
